meta.title: Notable pathogenic variants on consumer arrays
meta.description: The most conservative section. Only well-established pathogenic variants that are actually genotyped on 23andMe / AncestryDNA arrays. Alleles are on the GRCh38 forward (dbSNP reference) strand. Each row carries a ClinVar Variation ID and a citation.
meta.source: Alleles and pathogenicity verified against NCBI dbSNP (build 156) and NCBI ClinVar.
hard_disclaimer: This is NOT a diagnostic test and NOT medical advice.
A negative result does NOT rule anything out. Consumer arrays test a few specific spelling-changes, not whole genes; you can carry a disease variant this test does not look at.
A positive result is not a diagnosis. Array genotyping calls can be wrong and must be confirmed with clinical-grade testing.
Carrier status and low-penetrance risk are not the same as having, or being certain to develop, a disease.
Discuss any result here with a physician or a certified genetic counselor before acting on it.

excluded.APOE_alzheimers: APOE (rs429358 / rs7412) Alzheimer's-risk alleles are deliberately excluded from this section. Learning APOE status can have serious, non-actionable psychological consequences and is normally disclosed only with genetic counseling and explicit consent.

variants.inheritance: Autosomal recessive (two copies confer the main risk)

interpretations.2: Homozygous for C282Y (A/A): the classic high-risk genotype for hereditary haemochromatosis. Many, but not all, people with this genotype develop iron overload; penetrance is incomplete and it is treatable if caught. This warrants a conversation with a clinician about iron studies (ferritin, transferrin saturation).
interpretations.1: One copy of C282Y (carrier, G/A): usually unaffected. A single copy rarely causes overload on its own, but combined with an H63D copy (compound heterozygote) it can raise risk modestly.
interpretations.0: No C282Y allele (G/G): the C282Y variant was not found. This does NOT rule out haemochromatosis from other variants or genes.

variants.citation: Feder JN et al. A novel MHC class I-like gene mutated in hereditary haemochromatosis. Nat Genet (1996). PMID:8696333

variants.inheritance: Autosomal recessive; mainly relevant compound with C282Y

interpretations.2: Homozygous for H63D (G/G): usually low risk on its own; rarely causes significant iron overload without other factors.
interpretations.1: One copy of H63D (carrier, C/G): common and usually benign alone. Combined with a C282Y copy (compound heterozygote) it can modestly raise iron-overload risk.
interpretations.0: No H63D allele (C/C): the H63D variant was not found. This does NOT rule out haemochromatosis from other variants.

variants.citation: Feder JN et al. A novel MHC class I-like gene mutated in hereditary haemochromatosis. Nat Genet (1996). PMID:8696333
